verdicts.reason: Deliberate dependency-drop with a WHY comment recording the bounded format (bank settlement export, no embedded newlines) and an explicit revisit condition — exactly the rubric's don't-flag class for intentional re-implementation to avoid a new install/audit surface.

verdicts.replacement: Inconsistent patterns: the same YYYY-MM-DD formatting is done three different ways (manual getMonth/padStart, toISOString().slice(0,10), Intl.DateTimeFormat en-CA) — and they don't even agree (the ISO variant is UTC while the other two are local time, so results differ near midnight). Converge on one shared formatDateYmd helper; if local time is the intent, keep the Intl 'en-CA' 2-digit formatter and delete the other two.

Hand-rolled debounce, explicitly listed in the rubric's hand-rolled-primitives class, with no comment recording a deliberate tradeoff (contrast depdrop.ts, which has one). Replace with a maintained utility such as debounce from lodash-es or es-toolkit — noting the manifest is unverifiable so I cannot assert either is already installed; lower confidence than the other flags since a deliberate dep-drop rationale like depdrop.ts's would flip this to spare.

Hand-rolled deep-equal (rubric-listed primitive) that also silently mishandles Date, Map, Set, and RegExp values. If this runs on Node, replace with the stdlib's util.isDeepStrictEqual (zero new dependencies); otherwise a battle-tested micro-lib like fast-deep-equal.

verdicts.reason: Hand-rolled throttle, but the WHY comment records a deliberate choice to drop lodash-es for a single 8-line use, with a revisit condition — the rubric's explicit false-positive class for intentional dependency-drop re-implementation; note the tradeoff, don't flag.

CookieSessionStorage exists to satisfy supabase-js's SupportedStorage interface — an abstraction mandated by the library's auth-storage contract, not gratuitous indirection; the class is the minimal adapter shape that contract requires.

verdicts.replacement: Hand-rolled array group-by, explicitly listed in the rubric. Replace with the language's built-in Object.groupBy(items, keyFn) (ES2024) — a zero-dependency stdlib replacement; if the runtime target predates it, that constraint should be recorded, and none is.

Math.random()-chain string id — rubric-listed, and Math.random() is not collision-safe or unpredictable. Replace with the platform's crypto.randomUUID() (or crypto.getRandomValues for a custom alphabet/length), available in Node and browsers with no new dependency.

Over-abstraction: an interface + private class + factory wrapping one reduce, and the comment itself confirms a single call site with no second implementation planned — so this is an admission of speculative generality, not a recorded tradeoff. Collapse to a plain function: invoiceTotal(lineItems, invoiceId) returning (lineItems[invoiceId] ?? []).reduce((s, n) => s + n, 0).

Premature generality: a register/run plugin pipeline with module-level mutable state whose only registered transform lives in the same file. Replace with a direct function runExportPipeline(rows) returning rows.filter(row => row.deleted_at == null); reintroduce a registry only if a second, externally-registered transform ever materializes.

verdicts.reason: Plain domain logic: a pure proration calculation plus a straightforward fetch call, with the pure math split out as a testability seam; nothing here reimplements a stdlib/library primitive or adds indirection.

A simple single-pass domain aggregation over typed payment rows plus a Supabase query; the pure reconcileTotals/IO split is a testability seam, and a hand-written loop is the appropriate shape for a three-bucket tally — no primitive is being reinvented.
